source: must be in want of a wife
lost: The 'must' is inferential (it surely follows that he lacks one), but MUST means 'required' and strength particles are only allowed in a header, so an embedded proposition cannot carry epistemic necessity.
fix: Allow a strength particle in the modal slot of any clause (CERTAIN want ...), or define MUST as also 'necessarily so in fact', parallel to CAN.

source: a truth universally acknowledged
lost: IRONY marks the whole sentence, so the reader cannot tell that the irony sits on 'universally acknowledged truth' rather than on the embedded claim, nor what is meant instead.
fix: Allow attitude particles in the focus slot before one phrase, as strength already is.

source: However little known the feelings or views of such a man may be
lost: The universal concessive over a degree ('no matter how little') becomes a plain 'although barely known'.
fix: Allow ANY in the degree slot (ANY known = known to whatever degree), used inside DESPITE.

source: such a man ... he is considered
lost: A generic or variable introduced in one sentence cannot be picked up in the next, because NAMED on a quantified phrase binds only to the end of its sentence and THAT means an already identified individual.
fix: State that a handle bound on a GENERIC/ANY/SOME phrase stays live for later sentences that relate to it (DETAIL, RESULT, UNDER), or add a quantifier meaning 'of the kind just described'.

source: on his first entering a neighbourhood
lost: 'For the first time' needs a detour through 'ORD 1 time KIND { ... }' because ORD only precedes a noun-like head.
fix: Allow ORD n in the aspect slot (ORD 1 enter = enter for the first time).

source: so well fixed ... that he is considered
lost: The degree-result link (the extent itself brings about the result) is split into VERY plus a separate RESULT sentence.
fix: Add a result role (see D20 'for breezy conditions') that VERY/TOO-type degrees can take with a block.

source: It is a truth universally acknowledged ...
lost: It is unclear whether a fictional narrator's general statement is CLAIM (asserted) or STORY (not asserted); only one opener is allowed.
fix: Say that STORY covers narrator commentary, or allow BY narrator with a normal opener inside a STORY text.

source: Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.
lost: The spec uses BY for both direct and reported speech, so verbatim quotation and indirect report cannot be told apart.
fix: State the convention: a BY block is the speaker's own words; a bare block under a speech root is an indirect report.

source: "But it is," returned she; "for Mrs. Long has just been here"
lost: A quotation of two sentences with different openers and a relation between them cannot be encoded cleanly, because blocks carry no labels and a relation inside a block targets the previous top-level sentence.
fix: Allow a label inside a block ({ BY W a: ... }) and let a relation with no target inside a joined block point at its left sibling.

source: Do not you want to know who has taken it?
lost: The negative question expects 'yes', but CERTAIN/LIKELY/POSSIBLE after ASK have no polarity, so the expected answer is not recoverable.
fix: Let ASK take YES or NO (optionally with a strength) as the expected answer.

source: have you heard that Netherfield Park is let
lost: A bare block is 'mentioned, not asserted', so the speaker's commitment to the embedded fact under a factive verb is not marked.
fix: State that a block under a GIVEN header inside the complement marks it as presupposed true.

source: his lady ... My dear Mr. Bennet ... I have no objection to hearing it
lost: Period register, the interrupted quotation and the dry understatement survive only as JEST and plain roots.
fix: none: out of scope

source: No Person shall be a Representative
lost: The sentence enacts a rule of eligibility; CLAIM presents it as an assertion without source and MUST NOT as a prohibition on the person.
fix: Add an opener (e.g. RULE) for norms that hold by being stated, usable with MUST/MAY/CAN.

source: who shall not have attained ... and been ..., and who shall not ... be an Inhabitant
lost: NOT cannot take scope over two joined clauses, so the literal 'not (A and B)' had to be replaced by the interpreted 'not A or not B', hiding a real ambiguity of the source.
fix: Allow ( ) to group clauses, with NOT, a modal or shared roles written outside the group.

source: No Person shall be
lost: The relative scope of a clause modal or NOT and a quantifier in a role phrase is not defined (MUST NOT ... ANY person vs MAY ... NONE person).
fix: Add one rule: clause-level NOT and modal outscope quantifiers in role phrases unless EACH is used.

source: No Person ... who ... he shall be chosen
lost: NAMED must follow all modifiers, yet the handle is needed inside those modifiers when relative clauses nest, so the handle is used before it is bound.
fix: Allow NAMED directly after the head, before the linkers.

source: there may exist valid reasons ..., but the full implications must be understood
lost: Clauses inside a block can be joined only by AND/OR, so the contrast is expressed with DESPITE, which reverses which half is foregrounded.
fix: Allow a relation particle (CONTRAST, CONCEDE, RESULT) before a non-first clause, targeting the clause to its left.

source: One vendor may choose ... another vendor may omit
lost: English 'may' is used loosely between permission and possibility; the encoding must pick MAY, CAN or POSSIBLE each time.
fix: none: out of scope (document CAN as the neutral choice)

source: truly optional
lost: 'Truly' (genuinely, no hidden obligation) is rendered as FULL, a degree of completeness; EMPHASIS is not available inside a block.
fix: Allow EMPHASIS in the focus slot before a predicate or phrase.

source: should be understood and the case carefully weighed before implementing any behavior
lost: A modal, a time clause and a concession shared by two clauses with different themes must be repeated on each clause or silently attach to one.
fix: Allow ( ) to group clauses, with shared roles after the group.

source: 3. SHOULD ... 5. MAY
lost: The text defines its own SHOULD and MAY, but a term defined with DEFINE cannot afterwards stand in the modal slot, so later normative sentences would silently use the language's built-in SHOULD and MAY instead.
fix: Allow a handle or « » term bound by DEFINE to fill the modal slot.

source: (or at least not forwards)
lost: The scalar fallback 'at least' (if not the stronger claim, then this weaker one) has no particle; ATLEAST is for numbers only.
fix: Allow ATLEAST in the focus slot before any phrase.

source: DID NOT TOUCH ... AT ALL / _any_ / *any* / literally / completely
lost: Shouting, stress and intensifying adverbs all collapse into EMPHASIS, FOCUS and FULL, so the graded heat of the message flattens.
fix: none: out of scope (or let EMPHASIS take VERY)

source: Honestly, ... / The fact is, ... / literally
lost: Adverbs that comment on the speech act (speaking frankly, not exaggerating) have no slot; they are dropped or folded into CERTAIN and EMPHASIS.
fix: Add one attitude particle FRANK; allow EXACT in the degree slot for 'literally'.

source: what you have been doing is basically saying "as a DMA maintainer I control ..."
lost: The quoted words are the writer's hostile paraphrase of the addressee's stance, but a BY YOU block presents them as something the addressee actually said.
fix: Allow a strength or UNREAL directly after BY (BY YOU UNREAL { ... }) to mark words put in someone's mouth.

source: basically saying
lost: 'Basically' (in essence) has only ALMOST, which wrongly implies falling short; AROUND is for numbers only.
fix: Allow AROUND in the degree slot.

source: is basically saying
lost: 'X amounts to Y' needs a comparison between two things, but THAN is a clause role and EQUAL needs a gradable predicate, so identity or equivalence of two phrases has no licensed form.
fix: State that EQUAL alone may be a predicate: EQUAL THEME x THAN y.

source: just another user of it
lost: 'Another' means one more of the same kind; OTHER means a different one, so the additive sense needs ALSO 1.
fix: Document ALSO before a quantified phrase as 'one more'.

source: I control what the DMA code is used for
lost: An embedded wh-clause that is not a question still needs an ASK header because WHAT is only defined under ASK.
fix: Say what WHAT means in a block with no ASK, or allow ANY thing KIND { ... SELF } as the stated free-relative form.

source: has continued to expand ... remains low
lost: STILL is defined as continuing against an expectation of ending, yet the spec's own example uses it for neutral 'remains', so plain continuation is either unmarked or over-marked.
fix: Define STILL as plain continuation and leave counter-expectation to SURPRISE or DESPITE.

source: has moved up but remains low
lost: Because relations target whole sentences, every 'X but Y' inside a sentence forces a split into extra labelled sentences.
fix: Allow a relation particle before a non-first clause (same fix as D11).

source: roughly in balance
lost: The hedge 'roughly' has no non-numeric form; ALMOST says the balance is not quite reached, which the source does not say.
fix: Allow AROUND in the degree slot.

source: to 4-3/4 to 5 percent
lost: UPTO joins only bare digits, so a range with fractions or units must be dumped whole into « » and is opaque to the decoder.
fix: Allow UPTO between any two numbers or « » values, and a unit root after the range.

source: risks to achieving its ... goals / progress on inflation / target range for the federal funds rate
lost: Noun complements have only KIND, OF and REL, and the spec does not say which to use when an event noun keeps an argument, so the same relation can be written three ways.
fix: Allow role particles as linkers inside a phrase (risk TO x, progress ABOUT x).

source: mainly remain confined south of Seattle, and especially south of WA/OR border
lost: MAINLY covers both 'mostly' and 'especially', so the two-step grading (mostly here, and above all there) is flattened to two equal MAINLY phrases.
fix: Allow a degree before a focus particle (MOST MAINLY = especially), or split MAINLY into two particles.

source: spreads northwards into Washington / moves onshore into California
lost: A direction and an end point both want TO, but a role may appear once per clause, so the direction is pushed into VIA or FROM.
fix: Add a role for direction without arrival (TOWARD).

source: for breezy conditions
lost: A result stated inside the clause has no role (FOR is purpose), so it needs its own sentence with RESULT.
fix: Add a role particle for result, taking a phrase or block.

source: by Thursday into Friday / Saturday into next week / early Wednesday
lost: WHEN is a point in time; 'no later than' and 'continuing into' need 'NOT after REL' and 'until REL (SOME part OF ...)', and the deadline sense of 'by' is blurred.
fix: Allow UPTO between two time phrases and ATMOST before a time phrase for 'by'.

source: gusts over 30 MPH
lost: A comparison inside a modifier needs THAN, which the phrase grammar does not admit, so a full relative block is required; there is also no strict 'more than n' number prefix.
fix: Extend modifier to [degree] root [THAN phrase], and add OVER / UNDER beside ATLEAST / ATMOST.

source: NBM probabilities ... around 30-60%
lost: A numeric probability belonging to a named model cannot use the strength slot (that is the writer's own), so it becomes a predicate over a 'probability OF { ... }' phrase.
fix: Document BY source with LIKELY «range» as the form for third-party probabilities.

source: upper 40s to low 50s
lost: Vague sub-ranges of a decade have no number form and go verbatim into « ».
fix: none: out of scope (AROUND 47 UPTO 53 is close enough)

source: A deep upper low in the NE Pacific
lost: A place attached to a noun has no linker, so it is written as KIND (inside REL ...), which reads as a type of low rather than a location.
fix: Allow AT (and other role particles) as linkers inside a phrase.

source: Drier conditions by Thursday into Friday.
lost: The verbless telegraphic forecast style must be expanded into full clauses.
fix: none: out of scope

source: hey / nope / nah / ugh / lol / cool / btw
lost: Casual register is not markable; POLITE is the only register particle, so the chat decodes at the same level as the bank statement.
fix: Add one attitude particle CASUAL (and perhaps FORMAL).

source: we fixed *a* migration
lost: The stress is on the article (some migration, not this one); FOCUS before the phrase puts the stress on the whole phrase, so the point of the joke is blurred.
category: focus on part of a phrase
fix: State that a focus particle written directly before a quantifier or modifier scopes to that word only.

source: need a hand or should I leave you to it
lost: ASK over two clauses joined by OR can be read as a yes/no question about the disjunction or as a choice between the two.
fix: State that OR directly under ASK asks which one, and that a yes/no question over a disjunction must wrap it in a block.

source: thought we fixed that
lost: US is 'the writer's group' and ME AND YOU is the pair, so a team that includes the addressee and others has no exact form.
fix: Define US as neutral about the addressee, with US ALONG YOU and US EXCEPT YOU when it matters.

source: again??
lost: A one-word echo question on an aspect cannot be a fragment, so the whole clause has to be rebuilt.
fix: Allow a fragment to be a lone clause-slot particle that inherits the rest from the target sentence.

source: fixed that / this one's new
lost: THAT and THIS are quantifiers and need a head, so bare demonstrative pronouns require an invented noun (THAT problem).
fix: Allow THAT and THIS as heads.

source: some prime q divides N. But q cannot be ...
lost: A witness introduced by an existential needs a name that lasts through the proof, but NAMED after a quantified phrase binds only to the end of the sentence, so a separate DEFINE is needed.
fix: State that SOME x NAMED Q in an asserted sentence introduces a handle that persists (until the enclosing supposition closes).

source: infinitely many primes / only finitely many primes
lost: The spec's own example 'finite THEME ALL prime' decodes as 'every prime is finite'; there is no stated way to predicate something of a collection as a whole or to state its cardinality.
fix: Add a collective quantifier (e.g. WHOLE: the set taken together) or allow a quantity word as predicate: (MANY KIND NOT finite) THEME prime.

source: call them p1, p2, ..., pn
lost: Handles are single letters with no index, so a family of names and the list they form can only be written as opaque « » notation.
fix: Allow a handle with an index (P 1, P I) and P 1 UPTO P N for the list.

source: Let N = p1 p2 ... pn + 1. Since N > 1
lost: A formula in « » cannot stand as a sentence body, the Logic section names no functions (no product over a list), and BE is used in DEFINE but not listed as a particle.
fix: Allow «notation» as a predicate or whole body, and list the built-in functions or say that any root may be one.

source: Suppose, for contradiction,
lost: The purpose of the supposition belongs to the act of supposing, but a FOR role would attach to the supposed content; header-level adjuncts do not exist.
fix: Allow FOR phrase in the header after the opener.

source: q cannot be any of p1, ..., pn / leaves remainder 1
lost: Identity ('is the same thing as', 'equals 1') has no stated form: there is no 'is', and EQUAL is a degree needing a gradable predicate.
fix: State that (x) THEME y is identity, or let EQUAL stand alone as a predicate.

summary: The spec handles discourse structure, evidential source, proof scaffolding, dialogue turns and hedged institutional prose well; the central-bank text and the proof lost almost nothing of substance. Losses cluster in three places: (1) anything that must happen below sentence level, since relations, strength and attitude live only in the header, so clause-level 'but', embedded epistemic 'must', scoped irony and relations inside quoted speech all need splitting or workarounds; (2) scope and binding, where the spec is silent or too tight (NOT over joined clauses, modal versus quantifier, variables that die at the sentence end, collective versus distributive ALL); (3) small gaps in closed classes: non-numeric approximation, graded focus, a result role, direction versus goal, time intervals, and a marker for casual register. I used openers, relations, KIND/OF/REL, DONE/STILL/PAST/FUTURE, CAN/MUST, BY and NAMED constantly; I never used MUTUAL, EXCEPT, HABIT, STOP, RARE/NEVER, LEAST, TOO/ENOUGH, UNREAL, REGRET/GLAD, TOPIC, INSTEAD or the Logic slots, and UNREAL was missed only for the paraphrased quotation. The particle count felt manageable, but several near-neighbours needed the spec open to choose between (STILL versus ONGOING, MAY versus CAN versus POSSIBLE, OF versus REL versus KIND, DESPITE versus CONCEDE). Most proposed fixes reuse existing particles in new slots rather than adding new ones.
